title: IT manager operating rhythm
note: These are practitioner suggestions to adapt to your organisation, its size, its risks and its contracts. They are not standards. No frequency or duration here is stated or required by any law, regulation or standard. Where a contract, regulator or certification scheme applies to you, follow that source and the frequency it gives.

cadences.label: Daily
cadences.intro: A short routine that finds problems while they are small. About 80 minutes in total, much of it in the first hour of the day.

items.title: Overnight alerts and backup results
items.why: A failed backup or a quiet alert channel is easy to miss. Read the job results instead of assuming they ran.

items.title: Service desk queue and SLA breaches
items.why: Look at the oldest tickets, anything breached or about to breach, and who is stuck. Ageing tickets are where users lose trust.

items.title: Security alerts and unusual sign-ins
items.why: Check the security console or alert digest for anything that needs a decision, such as a new admin account or repeated failed sign-ins.

items.title: Change calendar for today and tomorrow
items.why: Know what is changing, who owns it and whether it collides with a busy business period. Stop or move a change that is not ready.

items.title: Expiring certificates, licences and domains
items.why: A glance at the list of items expiring in the next 30 days. Expiry outages are avoidable and embarrassing.

items.title: People check-ins
items.why: A few short conversations or messages: who is blocked, who is overloaded, who is out. Fix small blockers the same day.

items.title: Set the top three for the day
items.why: Pick the three results that would make today a good day, and say what will not happen. Use the day plan to check they fit.

items.title: End-of-day shutdown
items.why: Capture loose ends, update the task list, note handover points and set tomorrow's first task. See templates/end-of-day-shutdown.md.

cadences.label: Weekly
cadences.intro: Where priorities, people and spend are kept in line. Roughly four to six hours a week, mostly meetings you already have.

items.title: IT team meeting
items.why: Share priorities, incidents and changes, and agree who owns what. Keep it short and decision-led.

items.title: One-to-ones with direct reports (per person)
items.why: Regular, protected time for each person: workload, blockers, development and how they are. Cancelling them teaches the team what matters least.

items.title: Vendor actions and chasing
items.why: Review open supplier tickets, quotes and deliveries. Chase the ones that are late and record the answer.

items.title: Risk register review
items.why: Check new risks, changed ratings and overdue actions. Close or escalate, do not just re-read.

items.title: Budget and spend check
items.why: Compare committed and actual spend with the budget line by line for anything unusual, new subscriptions and unapproved purchases.

items.title: Patch and vulnerability status
items.why: How many devices and servers are behind, what is overdue, and what exceptions are open. Decide what is pushed this week.

items.title: Projects and change review
items.why: Status of live projects, upcoming changes and anything that needs a decision or more people.

items.title: Backlog tidy
items.why: Close stale tasks, split large ones, re-rate importance and make sure blocked items have an owner. See docs/time-blocking-for-it-managers.md.

items.title: Weekly review and next week's plan
items.why: Look at what was done, what rolled over and what is overdue, then plan next week. See templates/weekly-review.md.

cadences.label: Monthly
cadences.intro: Evidence, reporting and checks that something still works. Roughly eight hours a month.

items.title: KPI pack
items.why: Collect the handful of measures you track (for example availability, ticket volumes, SLA performance, patching and spend) and note what changed and why.

items.title: Board or leadership report
items.why: A one to two page update: what happened, what is at risk, what you need decided. See templates/monthly-leadership-update.md.
items.suggested_when: last working days of the month

items.title: Access review sample
items.why: Pick a sample of accounts and permissions, especially administrators, and confirm each is still needed. Record what you removed.

items.title: Licence and subscription review
items.why: Match paid licences and subscriptions to people and use. Reclaim or cancel what is idle.

items.title: Backup restore or DR test
items.why: Restore a real item from backup, or run one step of the recovery plan, and write down how long it took and what broke. A backup that has not been restored is a hope.

items.title: Budget forecast against actuals
items.why: Update the year-end forecast and explain variances to the finance partner before they ask.

items.title: Joiners, movers and leavers reconciliation
items.why: Compare the HR list of leavers and movers with accounts, devices and licences. Close the gaps.

items.title: Incident and problem review
items.why: Look for repeat incidents and near misses. Pick one cause to remove.

cadences.label: Quarterly
cadences.intro: Bigger conversations that need preparation. Roughly ten hours a quarter, more if you have several key suppliers to review.

items.title: Supplier reviews (key suppliers)
items.why: Review service, cost, risks and relationship with each key supplier, and agree actions. Do this before renewal dates, not after.

items.title: Policy review
items.why: Review a rotating share of IT policies so each one is read at least once a year. Retire the ones nobody follows.

items.title: Tabletop exercise
items.why: Walk the team through a realistic incident on paper: who does what, who is told and what decisions are needed. Record the gaps and fix them.

items.title: Roadmap and priorities review
items.why: Check progress against the plan, drop what no longer matters and confirm the next quarter's priorities with leadership.

items.title: Full risk register review
items.why: Rework the whole register with owners: ratings, treatments, accepted risks and new risks.

items.title: Privileged access review
items.why: Review all administrator and service accounts and their owners, not just a sample.

items.title: Lifecycle and capacity review
items.why: List hardware and software nearing end of support, and storage, network and licence headroom. Feed the budget.

items.title: Team development check
items.why: Review objectives, training, workload and succession for each role.

cadences.label: Annual
cadences.intro: Large pieces of work that need to be put in the diary months ahead.

items.title: Budget cycle
items.why: Prepare the next year's operating and project budget with evidence from the lifecycle review and the roadmap. Total effort, spread over several weeks.

items.title: Contract renewals calendar
items.why: Rebuild the list of every supplier contract with end date, notice period and owner, and set reminders well before each notice date.
items.suggested_when: once a year, then keep current

items.title: Full disaster recovery test
items.why: Run a complete recovery of a priority service in a safe way, time it and compare it with what the business expects. Total effort including preparation.

items.title: Certification and accreditation renewals
items.why: List every certificate, accreditation, training record and assurance report that expires, with the lead time to renew it.
items.suggested_when: once a year, then keep current

items.title: Strategy and roadmap refresh
items.why: Revisit the multi-year direction with leadership. Check it still fits where the business is going.

items.title: Third-party assurance requests
items.why: Ask critical suppliers for current evidence of how they protect your data and keep service running, and note what is missing.

items.title: Team training and succession plan
items.why: Agree development plans, cover for key people and the skills you need next year.
